npcs.name: Gate-Sergeant Ottey
npcs.title: The Drill Yards
dialog: Up here we don't ask why we keep the watch. The empire locked its door and left us on the step like a delivery nobody signed for. Fine. We're Caerdun. We signed for ourselves.
The wall's been walked every night for three hundred years and it will not stop being walked because my knees have opinions.
Harbour, lighthouse, ramparts, crown. Learn the city; the city is the route.

npcs.name: Paymaster Vail
npcs.title: The Wage Vaults
dialog: Nine generations of my family have kept this room. Every night of watch stood on that wall since the Sealing, written down, valued, and owed.
The empire left without paying its garrison. So we kept the invoice.
Touch nothing else; the vault notices.

npcs.name: Marshal Grett
npcs.title: The Drill Yards
dialog: FORMS! Wall-form third! Your grandmothers held this line with worse knees and better attitudes!
Our oath isn't fight. Our oath is hold until relieved. Nobody relieved us. So we hold.
I don't break oaths for civilians. So: stop being one.

npcs.name: Duelist-Master Sabel
npcs.title: The Drill Yards
dialog: First blood, all grievances discharged, drinks after. It's civilised, it's legal, and it keeps the lawyers poor, which I consider a public service.
People don't fight over old paper. They fight over paper that frightens them.
Composure is half of duelling and all of being a second. Practise on the walk.

npcs.name: The Lord Marshal
npcs.title: The Parade Square
dialog: Once as a soldier, once as a ruler, once as a man whose grandfather died on that wall. It reads differently each time and it never reads well.
Three cities, three pieces, three centuries of not comparing notes. That ends now.
If the empire truly means to settle its debts, what happens next is the largest transaction in the history of the world.

npcs.name: Armourer Brann
npcs.title: The Market Crossroads
dialog: Swords for the shield line, katanas for the duelling code, and chain for anyone who means to be hit and remain upright.
Three hundred years of drill and not one sword drawn in anger. The steel doesn't know that. Keep it oiled.
The court buys the garrison's kit from me on credit against the day the empire pays. I have a very long ledger and a very patient wife.

Robes. Staves. Wraps for people who punch things for a living. The court says every job buys at its own city's door now, so here they hang, between my good swords. Don't touch the chain with ink on your hands.

npcs.name: Chandler Mott
npcs.title: The Market Crossroads
dialog: Potions, salves, a coat that keeps the fjord out. If the wall wants it, I stock it; if the wall doesn't want it, someone's cousin does.
Fish carts yield for no one. You'll learn.

npcs.name: Broker Ashby
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: The auction house of Caerdun, chartered by the court, three percent to the treasury and not a copper more, whatever Moonmere charges.
Relics sell here. Relics also register with the court, for standing rather than gold. The court remembers who did which.

npcs.name: Broker Pike
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: Four counters, one ledger. List it with me or with Ashby, it goes up on the same board and the same buyer finds it.
The board is copied out fresh at every bell. If your price is pinned there, somebody on this floor has already argued about it.

npcs.name: Broker Tarrant
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: Moonmere's brokers bid in whispers. Ours call it across the floor; the court likes its trades heard.
Three in the hundred to the treasury. The court counts it twice and the garrison eats it once.

npcs.name: Broker Lang
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: Sea traders come up the Wall Stair with the hold still on their boots. Weigh it, price it, pin it to the board.
The balance on the belfry is the same sign over the house in Heartwood and in Moonmere. Coin keeps one language, whatever the courts speak.

npcs.name: Drillmaster Hal
npcs.title: The Paladin Hall
dialog: Shield line to the north hall, duelling code to the south, and the parade square between them where the two argue about which of them is Caerdun.
Every job is open to an explorer. Stand in the hall's light to take up another; the body remembers what the drill taught it.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Sayre
npcs.title: The Crown Inn
dialog: A bed, a bowl, and a fire that has not gone out since the Sealing. My family has a bet on with the wall about which lasts longer.
Envoys, freebooters, sergeants off shift. Everybody's somebody's story in here.

npcs.name: Guildmaster Torv
npcs.title: The Smiths' Guild
dialog: Iron from the Fields' seams, shell from the fen, antler from the wood. Bring me the makings and the guild will teach you the making. Press K to see what your hands know.
The empire's blades were better than ours. The empire's blades are also three hundred years away. Ours are here.

npcs.name: Lamp-Keeper Hilde Varn
npcs.title: The Lighthouse
dialog: Stand on my left if you want an answer. The right ear went to the fog bell when I was a girl, and the bell has said nothing since worth hearing twice.

Three hundred years the lamp has been lit for ships the empire meant to send. None came. The fishers steer by it anyway, and Hurst carries the oil up that stair twice a day and complains about it both ways.
The watch's sheet goes on the post, not in my hand. I'll sign it. And I heard you the first time.

npcs.name: Quartermaster Ingrid Kettle
npcs.title: The Halls' Stores
dialog: The halls' stores. Helms for the shield line, headguards for the duelling code, each one entered in the hall's account under your name. Boots are the doorstep's business.
The hall's account, your name, paid in full or not at all. The court has run on credit for three hundred years; my shelf does not.
Wear it when your job has earned the level. I sell early. The steel can wait for you; it has had practice.

npcs.name: Shield-Captain Thora Lund
npcs.title: The Shield Line
dialog: The shield line's terms are short. Hold until relieved. Three hundred years on, I can give you the shift count to the day; my father Bertil kept the tally before me and keeps it yet, retired, at the kitchen table.
A recruit's days of service are wages owed. I keep the hall's roll; Vail's vault gets the copy, and the empire can argue the rate when it gets home.
Paladin work is given out of this hall. Not by Hal; Hal teaches the body. I teach the terms.

npcs.name: Code-Master Eskil Rudd
npcs.title: The Duelling Code
dialog: The code is three pages. The commentary is four hundred. Sabel keeps the commentary and the yard; I keep the three pages and the hall.
A duel is a contract with a witness. Everything else that happens with a sword is weather.
My cousin grinds blades on Smiths' Lane. She says nobody brings her a dull one twice. That is the whole curriculum.

interactables.name: The Harbour Tower Watch
interactables.idle_msg: The Harbour Tower Watch, the watch post at the end of the south mole. A slate for the night's muster hangs by the door, three hundred years of chalk ghosts on it where every night's names have been written up and rubbed out.
interactables.active_msg: You hand over the first muster sheet. The watch officer signs for it without looking up from the quay; the fish carts yield for no one, and neither does the watch. One post done, three to go: the Lighthouse next.

interactables.name: The Lighthouse Watch
interactables.idle_msg: The Lighthouse Watch: Lamp-Keeper Hilde Varn's post at the tower's foot. She is deaf in her right ear. Stand on her left.
interactables.active_msg: The second sheet, signed for. Hilde Varn asks you to repeat yourself, then tells you she heard you the first time and was only checking you'd remembered which side to stand on. Next, the Sea Ramparts.

interactables.name: The Sea Ramparts Watch
interactables.idle_msg: The Sea Ramparts Watch, the post over the sea wall. The granite of its doorway has gone soft at the corners from three hundred years of shoulders leaning on it between rounds.
interactables.active_msg: The third sheet. The watch officer reads it twice, as the watch officer here always has, and files it under a stone that has held muster sheets since the Sealing, the night the border shut. One post left: the Crown Terrace.

interactables.name: The Crown Terrace Watch
interactables.idle_msg: The Crown Terrace Watch, the highest post on Caerdun's wall. Gate-Sergeant Ottey's father held it, and his father before him.
interactables.active_msg: The top sheet, signed for on the crown. From here you can see the whole city below, the road running east across the Caerdun Fields, and beyond it the mountains of the border: the thing this wall has watched for three hundred years. All four delivered; back down to Ottey at the Drill Yards.

interactables.name: Archive Volume: Year One
interactables.idle_msg: The deep vault's shelves on rails. This is the Archive Volume for Year One, the wage book's first volume: the night watch of the night the border shut. Its first page reads, in a steady hand: one night: owed.
interactables.active_msg: You lift volume one. The hand that wrote its first page did not shake. One of the three Paymaster Vail wants; the others are Year One Hundred and Fifty and Year Three Hundred.

interactables.name: Archive Volume: Year One Hundred and Fifty
interactables.idle_msg: The Archive Volume for Year One Hundred and Fifty, initialled on every page by the paymaster of the day. The halfway mark of a debt nobody expected to collect.
interactables.active_msg: You lift the volume. Halfway through three hundred years, and the garrison kept writing every night down. They kept going. One more to take to Vail's desk.

interactables.name: Archive Volume: Year Three Hundred
interactables.idle_msg: The Archive Volume for Year Three Hundred: this year's, the ink still bright on its newest page, which is last night's watch.
interactables.active_msg: You lift the last volume. Something is misfiled between its pages: a loose sheet on paper nothing like the rest, in a hand nothing like the rest, with a seal pressed at its foot. Bring all three to Paymaster Vail.

interactables.name: The Dueling Ground
interactables.idle_msg: The Dueling Ground: a ring of worn granite in the Drill Yards where Caerdun settles, under its duelling code, what the courts cannot. Two families, the Harrows and the Tallises, face each other across it, and Duelist-Master Sabel waits at its edge for her second.
interactables.active_msg: You stand at Sabel's left through the forms. First blood comes quickly. As it lands, a Harrow cousin's hand goes to a knife; your shoulder is already in the way, and the knife stays where it is. Honour served, all grievances discharged. The Tallis boy hands Sabel a folded paper, the schedule, with visible relief.

interactables.name: The Sealed Imperial Clock
interactables.idle_msg: The clock tower beside the court hall. Behind a grate below its bell floor stands the Sealed Imperial Clock, the only imperial thing in Caerdun that still runs: nobody in the city has ever been able to stop it or set it, and its dials show a count, not an hour.
interactables.active_msg: You copy the dial-count through the grate, touching nothing. Set beside the schedule's final entry, the numbers agree: the clock is counting down to the same day. Of course it agrees; it's theirs. Take the numbers back to Paymaster Vail in the Wage Vaults.

court_archive.name: Wage Vaults in the Court Hall

npcs.name: Chanter Ives
npcs.title: The Song-Steps
dialog: Stop slouching, you'll dent the note before you've sung it.
In this city we keep everything in songs: law, land, grudges, recipes. Paper burns and stone gets carted off by empires, but a song lives in too many chests to steal.
The trees fined a man last spring. Well. We fined him. On their behalf.

npcs.name: Mother Alder
npcs.title: The Song-Steps
dialog: You're none of you ready and also my tea is getting cold.
A promise you can't hurry will eat a city alive if you let it sit on the table. So we put it away until the counting was nearly done.
Somebody fetch my tea.

npcs.name: Grudge-Keeper Morrow
npcs.title: The Grudge Hall
dialog: Wipe your feet; the floor is grudges.
Every grove felled for their Estates, every family moved at pike-point for their Gardens. People call us bitter. We prefer accurate.
Grudge-keepers don't do religion, friend. We do appointments.

npcs.name: The Speaker of the Ring
npcs.title: The Grove Ring
dialog: It's rude to talk about the trees where they can't hear. Sit under the ring with me.
These elders were planted the night the empire vanished. Imperial stock: bred, not wild. Bred trees are bred for something.
Banning a thing means keeping a copy.

npcs.name: Tanner Wick
npcs.title: The Crossroads
dialog: Leather for the chanters, greatswords for the grudge-keepers, and wraps for anyone who'd rather hit a thing than sing at it.
Everything here was a boar or a tree first. Heartwood wastes nothing; it's a point of pride and a shortage of money.
Mail and robes on a tanner's rack. Heartwood buys for every job now, so I stock what Caerdun forges and Moonmere weaves, and I don't pretend to like the smell of oiled steel.

npcs.name: Grocer Nell
npcs.title: The Crossroads
dialog: Windfall, frog legs, potions the mending college won't admit it buys from us. Sit, eat, then buy.
The song for haggling has nine verses. I know all nine. You'll pay the price on the board.

npcs.name: Broker Fennick
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: Heartwood's auction house, under the ring's own trees. The court takes its cut and puts it back in the groves; that is the whole of our politics.
Grove-relics find eager buyers here. Sellers name their price; the court takes the same small cut on every sale. Heartwood remembers what the empire took.

npcs.name: Broker Rook
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: Four counters and one board. List it with me and Fennick can sell it, or Hazel, or Sedge; it is the same ledger.
Every sale is written twice here: once for the buyer, once for the groves. Heartwood keeps receipts. It has kept them for three hundred years.

npcs.name: Broker Hazel
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: Imperial silver fetches what it weighs. Grove-relics fetch what they cost us, and the court sees to it that they do.
The balance in the hoop over the dome is the same sign as the one over Caerdun's house and Moonmere's. Coin keeps one language, whatever the courts speak.

npcs.name: Broker Sedge
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: The board is copied fresh at every chant. If your price is pinned there, somebody on this floor has already argued about it.
The court takes its small cut on every sale and plants it back in the groves. The planting rolls are open to anyone who asks the Ring.

npcs.name: Chant-Master Wynn
npcs.title: The Chanters' Hall
dialog: The chanters' hall keeps the war-songs the empire banned, and the grudge hall across the ring keeps the reasons. Between them, the two jobs this city gave the world.
Stand in the hall's light and any job is yours to take up. A song lives in too many chests to steal; so does a skill.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Tamsin
npcs.title: The Elder's Rest
dialog: A bed under the elder's boughs and stew that has a verse of its own. Sing it if you like; the stew doesn't mind.
The mourning trees budded this spring. Every one. The inn's been full of people pretending not to look up.

npcs.name: Woodwright Hollis
npcs.title: The Woodwrights' Guild
dialog: Leatherwork, weaving, the shaping of what the wood gives. Bring the guild hides and resin and it will teach you the rest. Press K to see what your hands know.
The empire planted its Estates in rows. We plant where the seed falls. Both make timber; only one makes a song.

npcs.name: Outfitter Bryn Hollow
npcs.title: The Grove Ring Outfitter
dialog: Headbands for the chanters, visors for the grudge-keepers. Cut on the Grove Ring, fitted by eye, never twice the same.
The chanters pay in verses and the grudge hall pays on Thursday. You pay now.
Grow into it before you wear it. Heartwood doesn't hurry a tree, and I don't hurry a fitting.

npcs.name: Reckoner Hale Thorn
npcs.title: The Grudge Hall
dialog: Morrow keeps the floor. I keep the dates. Every grudge on the floor has a date against it, the date is an appointment, and a dark knight is what keeps it.
You'll be told we're bitter. Bitter is a flavour. We're a ledger.
Don't tell me a thing was settled unless you can show me the receipt.

npcs.name: Refrain-Master Ione Larch
npcs.title: The Banned Refrain
dialog: Shoulders down. Breath first, then the note, then the fist. Every chanter who ever won did it in that order.
The empire banned the war-songs by proclamation, read from the Capital's gate. We kept them anyway. This hall is the proof: every verse still lives in a chest that breathes.
Wynn teaches the job. I keep the refrains, and I hand them out one at a time to those who've earned them.

interactables.name: The North Elder's Tally Post
interactables.idle_msg: The North Elder's Tally Post: a board at the foot of the north tree of the Grove Ring, where the tree's flowering is to be marked. Overhead, pale buds are opening on the low bough.
interactables.active_msg: Budded, every branch. You mark the North Elder on the board and turn sunwise. Next: the East Elder's Tally Post.
interactables.label: NORTH ELDER

interactables.name: The East Elder's Tally Post
interactables.idle_msg: The East Elder's Tally Post: a board at the foot of the east tree of the Grove Ring, where the tree's flowering is to be marked. Overhead, pale buds are opening on the low bough.
interactables.active_msg: Budded, the same as the north tree. You mark the East Elder on the board. Next sunwise: the South Elder's Tally Post.
interactables.label: EAST ELDER

interactables.name: The South Elder's Tally Post
interactables.idle_msg: The South Elder's Tally Post: a board at the foot of the south tree of the Grove Ring, where the tree's flowering is to be marked. Overhead, pale buds are opening on the low bough.
interactables.active_msg: Budded, all together, all at once, like the other two. You mark the South Elder on the board. Somebody planted a clock. Next sunwise: the West Elder's Tally Post.
interactables.label: SOUTH ELDER

interactables.name: The West Elder's Tally Post
interactables.idle_msg: The West Elder's Tally Post: a board at the foot of the west tree of the Grove Ring, where the tree's flowering is to be marked. Overhead, pale buds are opening on the low bough.
interactables.active_msg: Budded. You mark the West Elder, and the circle closes: four trees, one week, after three hundred years. The count matches the counting-song's years, verse for verse. Take the board back to the Speaker under the ring.
interactables.label: WEST ELDER

npcs.name: Archivist Junn
npcs.title: The Returns Desk
dialog: Oh good, hands. We're drowning in returns.
I love this place, but the catalogue lies. There's a shelf in the master index, row nine hundred, annex, that I have never found. Not lost. The index updates.
Especially don't show the Provost. Especially especially don't show the Provost.

npcs.name: Warden Liss
npcs.title: The Mending College
dialog: We treated the ones who reached the shore by dawn. No wounds to speak of. What they needed mending was elsewhere.
To us the shore families recite. To a stranger they have to actually remember.
Things that end violently are loud. Things that leave on schedule are quiet.

npcs.name: Master Corvo
npcs.title: The Burned Shelf
dialog: My college takes its name from a fire. We teach fire magic in the room where it happened, which the Provost calls economy and I call a confession with seating.
Burned books drown badly. The Mere, unlike this institution, keeps everything.
Ruin is legible if you went to school long enough.

npcs.name: Provost Selk
npcs.title: The Observatory
dialog: I hear excellent things, which always worries me; excellence is so rarely convenient.
An archive is not for remembering; any attic remembers. An archive is for deciding when.
Every Provost gets one night to be furious. In the morning, wind the clock.

npcs.name: Outfitter Quill
npcs.title: The Causeway Road
dialog: Staves, cudgels, and robes cut for people who read while they walk. The academy's colours are optional; the academy's prices are not.
Every scholar in the south walks the causeway once and rides the crystal ever after.
Yes, that is mail. No, I don't handle it; I fold it with tongs. The academy says every job gets its kit at every gate, and the academy pays the rent.

npcs.name: Sundries-Keeper Ada
npcs.title: The Causeway Road
dialog: Ink, ether, potions, and something for the damp; everything on this island is something for the damp.
The Provost's office buys its permit stamps from me. Four kinds. I have never asked why.

npcs.name: Broker Sennet
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: Moonmere's auction house, with the academy's tax on it and the academy's records of it. Documents fetch more here than anywhere; the college begs for paper.
Register a relic with the court instead and your name goes on the plaque. Names last longer than gold, on this island.

npcs.name: Proctor Elm
npcs.title: The Mending College
dialog: The mending college heals, the burned shelf burns, and the academy pretends the two have nothing to do with each other. Both jobs are taught here to anyone who asks.
Stand in the college's light to take up another job. Rest here too; the college mends what the road did.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Rue
npcs.title: The Shelf Inn
dialog: A room over the water and the sound of the causeway all night. Scholars sleep through it; you'll learn.
Three envoys left from this inn for the North Road on one morning, each swearing they'd tell nobody. I keep an inn. Nobody tells nobody.

npcs.name: Alchemist Imre
npcs.title: The Alchemists' Guild
dialog: Alchemy, and the cooking the academy insists is a different discipline. Lamproot, gels, pearls; bring the guild its makings and press K to see what you can brew.
The burned shelf next door computed something and then burned its own arithmetic. Alchemists never burn a result. We bottle it.

npcs.name: Merle Tarrant
npcs.title: Night Observer
dialog: The room above this one has louvres. They were painted over the week the empire went quiet, and the Provost's office renews the paint every year, in writing. I keep the night log one floor under it. The log has a column for the sky and no column for the room.

npcs.name: Kit Glazier
npcs.title: Lens Grinder
npcs.home: The Crown · the Precinct, west house

npcs.name: Tansy Scrivener
npcs.title: Letter Writer
npcs.home: The West Arm · the Scriveners' Row (WR1)

npcs.name: Yarrow Platt
npcs.title: Herb Dryer
npcs.home: The College Arm · the herb dryer (E3)

npcs.name: Under-Bursar Odile Vellum
npcs.title: The Bursar's Office
dialog: The Bursar is at lunch. The Bursar has been at lunch since the previous Provost. I am the Under-Bursar, and I am not.
Veils for the Mending College, hats for the Burned Shelf. The college's gown and the shelf's hat are both charged to your tuition, receipted in triplicate.
Footnote: refunds are paid at one quarter. The other three quarters are, in the college's words, education.

npcs.name: Dean Isolde Fairlie
npcs.title: The Mending College
dialog: Liss will have told you what they needed mending was elsewhere. She stops there. The rest of that sentence is the college's, and the college is the White Mage guild, and the guild has a ladder. See footnote one: you are standing on its first rung.
Elm teaches the job to anyone who asks. The college decides who wears its cloth. Those are different lists, and I keep the second one.

The date? The infirmary log for that night is in my desk. The page is fine. Ask me something I can answer. And no, the tallier at the harbour is not my doing; she is my cousin, and she counts better than I do.

npcs.name: Reader Corin Thrale
npcs.title: The Burned Shelf
dialog: Reader is the rank below Master and above anyone who still believes the syllabus was lost. It was burned. There is a difference, and I teach it.
Corvo teaches the fire. I teach what it was for. The shelf is the one place in the academy where the footnotes outlived the text.
Black Mage is a job, not a temperament, whatever the Provost says. Come back when you have one, and I will have a lamp that needs feeding.

npcs.name: Broker Quaile
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: Four counters and one ledger, and the academy reads the ledger. List it with me or with Sennet; it goes up on the same board and the same buyer finds it.
The board is copied out fresh at every bell, in a clerk's hand. Moonmere trusts nothing it cannot footnote.

npcs.name: Broker Fenwright
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: Caerdun's brokers call their prices across the floor. Here we bid in whispers and write them down; the academy likes its trades legible.
The academy's tithe is taken on every sale and entered twice, once in the ledger and once in the Registry. Nobody on this island has ever lost a receipt.

npcs.name: Broker Corbel
npcs.title: The Auction House
dialog: Sea goods come up the Mere Stair with the harbour still on them. Weigh it, price it, pin it to the board.
The balance in the roundel over the court is the same sign as the one over Caerdun's house and Heartwood's. Coin keeps one language, whatever the courts speak.

interactables.name: The Moon Stack
interactables.idle_msg: The Moon Stack: a heap of returned books, each slip marked with one moon, which means the upper shelf. Someone gave the whole of the second century's poetry back damp.
interactables.active_msg: Shelved on the upper shelf, the damp ones facing the window to dry. Now the Two-Moon Stack on the shelf below.

interactables.name: The Two-Moon Stack
interactables.idle_msg: The Two-Moon Stack: returned books whose slips carry two moons, which means the lower shelf.
interactables.active_msg: Shelved on the lower shelf. Nothing further damp. Only the ferry crates at the Causeway Landing remain.

interactables.name: The Ferry Crates
interactables.idle_msg: Crates unloaded from the causeway ferry at the landing, still wet. The books inside are returns, and one slip in the top crate carries three moons: a mark for a collection the academy says it does not have.
interactables.active_msg: The three-moon slip. Where the book belongs it says: row nine hundred, annex. The shelf Junn has never found. Quietly, then: take it to her at the Returns Desk.

interactables.name: The Registry Stamp
interactables.idle_msg: The registry's stamp, on a chain, beside the box of winter permit renewals. The Provost's order: registry first, then the bursar, then the harbourmaster across the causeway.
interactables.active_msg: Stamped, every form. Registry first. The order has always mattered. Next, the Bursar's Stamp beside this desk.
interactables.label: REGISTRY

interactables.name: The Bursar's Stamp
interactables.idle_msg: The bursar's stamp. The bursar is at lunch and has been, by the dust, since the previous Provost. The stamp works regardless.
interactables.active_msg: Stamped, every form. Bursar second. Now across the causeway to the Harbourmaster's Stamp at the Causeway Head on the Shores.
interactables.label: BURSAR

interactables.name: The Annex Door
interactables.idle_msg: Behind the star-globe on the observatory stair, a door with no shelf-mark and no number. Row nine hundred, annex, if Junn is right. Someone has dusted it.
interactables.active_msg: The key turns clockwise. Beyond it, the telescope room: every telescope inside is trained on the same empty point of sky, and a water-clock is running.

npcs.name: Proctor Anselm
npcs.title: Causeway Proctor
dialog: Explorers to the left of the gate, fares to the right. The academy keeps the road; it does not keep the water.
Three hundred years the north gate has been shut. Stand there long enough and you will hear the hinges thinking about it.

npcs.name: Ferrymaster Vey
npcs.title: The Gulf Crossing
dialog: We sail every ten minutes. Seven on the gulf, three at the pier. Speak to me while the ship is docked to put your name down.
The fare is what it is. If Moonmere wants it cheaper, Moonmere can pay the difference — they have before.

npcs.name: Cutter Bram
npcs.title: The Reed Harvest
dialog: Every ledger in the college started out standing in that water. Cut, dried, split, pressed.
The old harvest was imperial work. You can still see where they drove the stakes — in rows, of course. They did everything in rows.

npcs.name: Student Wen
npcs.title: Of the Reed Flats
dialog: I am to measure the flats every seventh day and write down what I find. What I find is water, and reeds, and a great many frogs.
The Provost says a shore is a clock if you read it slowly enough. I would rather read a book.

npcs.name: Watch-Sergeant Haldis
npcs.title: The North Gate
dialog: The gate opens when the court says it opens and not one morning sooner. Do not lean on it.
Beyond that wall is the Summer Lakes, and beyond those, the whole of an empire that went out and left the lamps burning.

npcs.name: Mereth, the Ferryman's Granddaughter
npcs.title: The Ferry Piers
dialog: My grandmother was on the water the night the far shore went quiet. She told it the same way every winter of my childhood.
Hushed is a held breath. Finished is a door. She said the difference is the whole story, if you're listening.

npcs.name: Lamp-Keeper Orla
npcs.title: The Point
dialog: The point's lamp was my family's before the academy took it over, and we kept it anyway.
The lamp book's entry for that night ends mid-word. Nobody in my family has ever finished the sentence.

npcs.name: Reed-Seller Mab
npcs.title: The Causeway Stalls
dialog: Reed hats, reed coats, and a little mail for anyone walking the shore road. Everything on this stall has crossed the causeway at least twice.
Potions too. The frogs don't bite, but the herons do, and the students never believe me until they've met one.

interactables.name: The Harbourmaster's Stamp
interactables.idle_msg: The harbourmaster's stamp at the Causeway Head, beside the board of ferry fares. The third and last stamp the winter permits need.
interactables.active_msg: Stamped, every form. Harbourmaster third. The box is finished; take it back across the causeway to Provost Selk's desk at the Observatory.
interactables.label: HARBOUR • FARES

npcs.name: Watchman Dorran
npcs.title: Of the Landward Gate
dialog: Out or in? Either way, mind the road. The coaches don't slow for anyone.
Three farms, one ferry, one gate that never opened. That was the whole of the Fields, until this year.

npcs.name: Farmer Alys
npcs.title: The Watch Farms
dialog: The watch farms fed the garrison for three hundred years. Now they feed whoever pays, which is you, apparently.
Boars in the wheat again. If you're chartered for anything, be chartered for that.

npcs.name: Coachman Pell
npcs.title: Milestone Zero
dialog: Every road in the empire was measured from this stone. Zero. Everything else is a distance from here.
North-east for the North Road and the inn. South-east for the gate, if you've a charter. The coach takes either, for a fare; the crystal by the stone takes you further, for less, once it knows you.

npcs.name: Ferrymaster Coll
npcs.title: The Gulf Crossing
dialog: We sail every ten minutes. Seven on the gulf, three at the pier. Speak to me while the ship is docked to put your name down.
The empire never built a road round the gulf. Thought the sea was cheaper. They were right.

npcs.name: Gate-Warden Hesk
npcs.title: The Border Gate
dialog: Three hundred years my family watched this door. Opened on its own, one morning, like it had somewhere to be.
Beyond is the Hunting Wood. The king's rides, and something in the wood that keeps the visitors' list.

npcs.name: Orchardist Petta
npcs.title: The Wild Orchards
dialog: Wild, they call them. Wild! I prune every one. Old rows, gaps full of seedlings, not a straight line left that the empire would approve of.
Windfall's yours if you pick it up. The song's yours if you can learn it. The trees are mine.

npcs.name: Elder Hazel
npcs.title: At Her Orchard Gate
dialog: My grandmother folded a verse of the counting-song into the way she cored an apple. I can show you. Sit.
The empire took the groves and gave us receipts. Heartwood kept the receipts. That is the whole of our politics.

npcs.name: Old Tammon
npcs.title: By the Mill Brook
dialog: The wheel turns whether anybody grinds or not. I come down to make sure it's still true.
There's a verse that goes with the sound of the brook. Nobody sings it right who hasn't sat here.

npcs.name: The Widow Crake
npcs.title: On the Ridge Path
dialog: From up here you can see the whole of the Fields and none of the Estates. That is by design. Mine.
The gate opened at dawn. I watched it. Nobody pushed it.

npcs.name: Charcoal-Master Dask
npcs.title: The Charcoal Camps
dialog: Charcoal for the city's forges, three carts a week. The smoke you saw from the road is us.
Boars root up the clamps at night. If you're chartered for beasts, start there.

npcs.name: Gate-Warden Ilse
npcs.title: The Border Gate
dialog: Beyond this is the Timber Estates. Every grove the empire felled, planted back in rows. Go and look at what they did.
Three hundred years shut. Now it stands open like it was waiting for the coach.

npcs.name: Auntie Wren
npcs.title: The Halfway Inn
dialog: Sit. Eat. Whatever it is, it'll keep until you've eaten; things usually do.
Three envoys at my table on one night, each swearing they'd tell nobody. I've kept an inn forty years. Nobody tells nobody.

npcs.name: Duelist-Master Sabel
npcs.title: Of Caerdun
dialog: Caerdun's ledgers end in a dated settlement-in-full. Debts get settled when the debtor plans to be in the room.
The inn is neutral ground. That is the only reason three courts will sit at one table.

npcs.name: Grudge-Keeper Morrow
npcs.title: Of Heartwood
dialog: The mourning trees budded all at once this spring. Every one. A clock, if you know how to read a tree.
I add a stone to the cairn every time I pass. Someone should count them.

npcs.name: Archivist Junn
npcs.title: Of Moonmere
dialog: Every telescope in the room was aimed at one empty point of sky. And the date was written under each one.
I have never been this cold. I have also never been this far from a shelf. The two feel related.

npcs.name: Ostler Bram
npcs.title: The Inn Stable
dialog: Coach horses want walking after the pass, not standing. Mind the yard, they kick.
Wolves come down to the road in the deep of winter. The lamps keep them off the yard. Mostly.

npcs.name: Road-Warden Tesk
npcs.title: The Border Cairn
dialog: Heartwood's ground from this cairn east. Caerdun's from the old milestones west. The inn sits on neither, which is the point of it.
Something big walks the crescent above the tarn. Leaves prints like a man's, if a man were a house.

npcs.name: Coachman Aster
npcs.title: The Coach Halt
dialog: Moonmere side by dusk if the axles hold. They usually hold.
Every scholar in the south walks this road once and rides it ever after. Rides the crystal, these days. The horses don't mind; the horses were never asked.

npcs.name: Stall-Keeper Ren
npcs.title: The Coach Halt
dialog: Fruit off the strand, water from the well, and no questions about what's in your pack.
The wreck down the bay? Grain ship, imperial. Three hundred years and the sand hasn't finished with it.

npcs.name: Fisher Marn
npcs.title: The South-West Shore
dialog: Crab, mostly. The big ones come up out of the wreck at night, which is why I fish by day.
You can see the academy's towers from the boat on a clear day. They never look any closer.

npcs.name: Student Ovi
npcs.title: Bound for the Academy
dialog: Forty miles of road and every mile of it is warmer than the last. I was told the academy was cold. I think I was lied to.
There's a watch on the headland. Imperial. My tutor says every sentinel on the coast was withdrawn on the Night. Withdrawn where?

npcs.name: Beachcomber Sull
npcs.title: The Wreck
dialog: Grain. Every barrel that comes out of that hull is grain, and every one of them sprouts. Three centuries dry and it sprouts.
Something keeps the purser's cabin. I don't go in. You could go in.

npcs.name: Scout Bettany
npcs.title: Caerdun's Forward Camp
dialog: Chart the water, the sightlines, and anything with teeth. The court's supply trains follow whatever you draw.
I've been practising being boring. Boring gets a supply train through. Interesting gets it eaten.

npcs.name: A Sentinel
npcs.title: Household Grounds
dialog: You are trespassing on household grounds. This notice is the four hundred and eleventh I have issued. Compliance to date: zero.
I am instructed to add, in cases of repeated offence: please.

npcs.name: The Warden of the Mausoleum
npcs.title: The Visitors' List
dialog: Names, please, for the visitors' list. You are not on the schedule. No one is on the schedule.
You may proceed as mourners, unscheduled. The emperors are sleeping. Mind the third step.

npcs.name: Huntsman Orrin
npcs.title: The Lodge
dialog: The king's rides. Three of them, straight as a rule, so the king could see a stag from the lodge door. He never came.
The hounds are still here. Three hundred years of hounds, bred in the kennels by a sentinel that does not know it is over.

npcs.name: Pike
npcs.title: A Freebooter, Retired
dialog: Garrison's ours now. The wood had it first, and the wood can have it back when we're done.
Don't go in the tomb. Something in there takes your name down.

interactables.name: The Sealed Notice
interactables.idle_msg: The Emperors' Vault, under the dome at the Mausoleum's heart. On the empty bier where an emperor would lie, a notice under wax: the Sealed Notice, the founding writ of the Hunting Wood. Through the wax you can read it: The household departs this night and will return. Keep out. Keep well.
interactables.active_msg: You break the seal and lift the writ. The household departs this night and will return. Keep out. Keep well. One line, in a steady hand, and nothing else. The writ is yours, and the province's founding terms with it; take its words back to Scout Bettany at Caerdun's Forward Camp.

interactables.name: The Visitors' Register
interactables.idle_msg: Fresh ink waits beside a register open at its last entry. The date is almost three centuries old. The visitor signed only: sorry. Below it, the next line has been ruled with care.
interactables.active_msg: Fresh ink waits beside the visitors' register. The next line is still blank.

interactables.name: The Unfinished Ledger
interactables.idle_msg: Lamp oil received. Linen washed. The names read at dusk. The same entries, year after year. The final column — Household returned — remains empty.
interactables.active_msg: The household has not returned. The lamps have never gone out.

npcs.name: Scout Wenna
npcs.title: Heartwood's Forward Camp
dialog: Every tree in this province stands where a clerk told it to. Chart it anyway; the court wants it in our hand, not theirs.
Mark the water, the sightlines, and anything with teeth. The sentinels count as teeth.

npcs.name: A Sentinel
npcs.title: Household Grounds
dialog: You are trespassing on household grounds. This notice is the four hundred and eleventh I have issued.
Compliance to date: zero. I am instructed to add, in cases of repeated offence: please.

npcs.name: The Overseer's Automaton
npcs.title: Roll Call
dialog: Roll call. Shift the first: absent. Shift the second: absent. Shift the third: absent. Excused -- household business.
Are you the relief crew? You are not on the rota. Nobody is on the rota. I have kept the rota anyway. One must.

npcs.name: Hasp
npcs.title: The Timber Yards
dialog: Freebooter, logger, whatever pays. The flume still runs and the saw still cuts. The empire built to last, I'll give it that.
Don't stand in the felled block after dark. The stumps are wet with sap and something drinks it.

npcs.name: Ranger Tallow
npcs.title: The Gardens Road
dialog: Heartwood's groves stood here. Every one felled, every one replanted in a row. My grandmother could name the trees they cut.
West is the King's Gardens. Nothing there is wild either, and you'll be trespassing the moment you cross.

interactables.name: The Sealed Notice
interactables.idle_msg: The Sealed Notice: a single sheet under a wax seal on the overseer's desk, beside a shift rota three hundred years long with every shift marked absent. Through the wax you can read the hand: The household departs this night and will return. Keep out. Keep well.
interactables.active_msg: You break the seal. The founding writ of the Timber Estates, in the empire's own hand and under its own seal: The household departs this night and will return. Keep out. Keep well. The writ is yours, and with it the province's founding terms, to carry back to Scout Wenna at the forward camp.

raised_chamber.name: Floor levels, with the Overseer's desk platform

npcs.name: Scout Ilva
npcs.title: Moonmere's Forward Camp
dialog: Chart the doorstep. The court wants every villa on the registry marked, and every lake sounded.
Every record we pulled ends the same way: original terms retained at -- and then it names the ballroom.

npcs.name: A Sentinel
npcs.title: Household Grounds
dialog: You are trespassing on household grounds. This notice is the four hundred and eleventh I have issued.
Compliance to date: zero. I am instructed to add, in cases of repeated offence: please.

npcs.name: Boatwright Tess
npcs.title: The Boathouse Crescent
dialog: Three boathouses and every boat in them still floats. Imperial pitch. I'd sell my grandmother for the recipe.
The dome in the west mere is a ballroom. Under the water. People danced in it. I row past it and I don't look down.

npcs.name: A Caretaker Sentinel
npcs.title: Villa Registry
dialog: The villa is closed for the season. The season has been closed for three hundred and eleven years. Please use the promenade.
The household will return. The linen is aired weekly. You may admire the garden from the path.

npcs.name: Student Pell
npcs.title: The Lily Meres
dialog: I am to count the lilies and write down what I find. What I find is that they close at dusk and open at dawn, which is a clock, if you are the Provost.
Moonmere's telescopes point at one empty piece of sky. I asked why. I was shown the door. The door is why.

interactables.name: The Sealed Notice
interactables.idle_msg: A notice under wax on the bandstand, beside a music box that repeats one bar of a waltz under the water. This is the province's founding writ: the empire's own statement of what this land is and who may hold it. Through the wax it reads: The household departs this night and will return. Keep out. Keep well.
interactables.active_msg: You break the seal. The household departs this night and will return. Keep out. Keep well. The writ is yours, and the province's founding terms with it: carry its words back to Scout Ilva at Moonmere's Forward Camp.

interactables.name: The Dance Cards
interactables.idle_msg: Dance cards on the sideboard, filled in for a dance interrupted between one step and the next. The last card reads: final dance -- reserved, upon our Return.
interactables.active_msg: You read the last card again. Final dance -- reserved, upon our Return.

raised_chamber.name: The palace descent and the bandstand

npcs.name: Duelist-Master Sabel
npcs.title: The Joint Camp
dialog: We came down through the Hunting Wood, Heartwood came over the Gardens pass, and Moonmere -- how were the Canal Works, Junn?
Sound the lane before you take the boards out to the tower. Drowned villages are hard on boots and worse on dignity.

npcs.name: Grudge-Keeper Morrow
npcs.title: The Joint Camp
dialog: Flooded on purpose, if you ask me, which nobody has, so I'm saying it loudly.
A dam nobody's tended in centuries holding like the day it was poured. Write that down for the grudge hall.

npcs.name: Archivist Junn
npcs.title: The Joint Camp
dialog: Damp. Educational. The tower's floors are an archive -- every province's records, duplicated, sent here. The lowest stacks are still wet.
The bell strikes on the hour, under the water. The intervals shorten. I have the tally in my sleeve.

npcs.name: Poleman Grist
npcs.title: The Boardwalk
dialog: The boards are sound to the tower and no further. The village is shallow now, but sound each step: broken cellars still take the careless.
Three courts on one shore and nobody's drawn steel yet. Give it a week.

npcs.name: The Sluice-Keeper
npcs.title: A Sentinel of the Dam
dialog: The dam holds. The dam has always held. I inspect the crest at dawn and the bore at dusk, and I will do so until the household returns.
You may cross. Keep to the crest. The parapet is not for sitting on; it is for holding the valley in.

interactables.name: The Wax-Sealed Cabinet
interactables.idle_msg: A cabinet in the bell chamber, sealed with wax before the valley was flooded; whatever is inside was meant to be found dry, by someone, someday. Through the wax you can make out one page lying in it, and a bundle of rolled papers beside it.
interactables.active_msg: You break the wax and lift the page out. One line, written the night before the vanishing in a hand so calm it is almost rude: 'Seal it behind us.' Beside it lie the striking rolls, the bell's peal written out year by year; the gaps between the strokes grow shorter every year, closing on one date.

interactables.name: The Striking Rolls
interactables.idle_msg: The bell's record, roll on roll. It is not a bell. It is a clock face the size of a valley, and it is counting down.
interactables.active_msg: You take the striking rolls. Every court will want them; every court will read the same date.

npcs.name: A Gardener Sentinel
npcs.title: The Parterres
dialog: Mind the parterre, please. It was edged this morning. Cut flowers are not available; the beds are being brought to standard.
You may admire from the path. The path is for admiring from.

npcs.name: Duelist-Master Sabel
npcs.title: The Fountain Court
dialog: Survey the four parterres, follow the gardeners' carts, and find where the cuttings go. I'll wait by the fountain; someone should.
The carts run inward. Fresh cuttings, potted stock, crate after crate, all bound for the capital. They were a nursery.

npcs.name: Archivist Junn
npcs.title: The Fountain Court
dialog: The registry lists every bed by its stock and its purpose. The purpose column says: household. Every bed.
A garden kept for three hundred years for someone who is coming back. I find that I cannot hate it.

npcs.name: The Head Gardener
npcs.title: The Glasshouse
dialog: Phase three: stock for the capital's parks. Phase four is the panes. You are not on the work order. Please use the path.
The household will want it as they left it. Nothing here is wild. Nothing here will be.

npcs.name: Vell
npcs.title: A Cutting Thief
dialog: Three hundred years of royal cuttings and nobody guarding them but a machine with manners. I take a few. Heartwood pays.
The maze changes nothing; the Gardener just re-cuts it. But I know this week's way through.

interactables.name: The Nursery Work Orders
interactables.idle_msg: Work orders on the nurseryman's desk, stamped and countersigned: cuttings and potted stock to be grown here and carted to the capital. The heading on every sheet reads 'Stock for the capital's parks, phase three, for the Restoration, by order of the Regent.'
interactables.active_msg: You take the top sheet. 'Phase three, for the Restoration, by order of the Regent.' Somebody inside the capital is still signing orders, and the Gardens have been growing a city's parks for three hundred years. Every court will want to read this.

raised_chamber.name: The cellar descent and the Nurseryman's office platform

portals.name: The Stair to the Border Wall

npcs.name: Warden Morrow
npcs.title: The Racking Yard
dialog: Six furnaces, never banked, three hundred years. Somebody is paying for the coal. Read the ledger and tell me who.
Panes. Crated, stencilled, counted. A city's worth of windows, and the city has no people in it. Yet.

npcs.name: Junn
npcs.title: The Racking Yard
dialog: The manifest on the table: 'To the capital of Vanai. Window replacements, phase four.' Phase four, Morrow. There were three before it.
Somebody is preparing a house for a guest. I would like to know who the guest is.

npcs.name: A Furnace Sentinel
npcs.title: The Furnace Row
dialog: The row is not to be approached during the pour. The pour is continuous.
Panes are counted at the rack. Shortfalls are recorded.

npcs.name: Pane-Seller Dorrit
npcs.title: Freebooter
dialog: Sentinels count the panes at the rack. They don't count the ones that never reach it. Buying?

npcs.name: A Stair Warden
npcs.title: The Wall Stair
dialog: The Border Wall's at the top. Watch where you put your feet; the glass on the steps is the real kind.

interactables.name: The Furnace Manifest
interactables.idle_msg: A manifest on the ledger table, weighted with a lump of cullet: 'To the capital of Vanai. Window replacements, phase four.'
interactables.active_msg: You copy the line. Phase four. Junn reads it over your shoulder and says nothing for a while.

interactables.name: The Furnace Ledger
interactables.idle_msg: The furnace ledger on its stand, three centuries of pours in one hand. The last page: 'To the capital of Vanai. Window replacements, phase four. By order of the Regent, for the Restoration.'
interactables.active_msg: You take the last page. Phase four, for the Restoration, by order of the Regent. The city is being readied for somebody.

raised_chamber.name: Floor levels, with the pour ledger office

npcs.name: Duelist-Master Sabel
npcs.title: The Expedition's Camp
dialog: The fen. Wonderful. I want it noted that I'm wearing my good boots, and that I blame the empire personally.
We can't get the boats past the old lock stair while it's fouled. Work down the lock line east of the sluice: clear the three drowned locks, and pull a copy of every repair order nailed to the posts.

npcs.name: Warden Morrow
npcs.title: The Lock Line
dialog: They will mend a canal for the homecoming. The groves they took from my families have waited three centuries for one sapling of restitution, but the barges must run on time.
Leave me be a moment. I'm going to stand in this mud and be exactly as angry as this deserves.

npcs.name: Junn
npcs.title: The Paperwork Barge
dialog: A barge full of three-hundred-year-old paperwork, and I'm not allowed to talk about how happy that made me. Manifests, tolls, lock tallies. The canal company's whole life.
Hear the water moving? The sentinels have started repairing the works. Three centuries of letting the fen drown itself, and this season they're dredging.

npcs.name: A Dredge Sentinel
npcs.title: The Great Sluice
dialog: The works are under repair. Navigable by the Restoration. Stand clear of the paddles.
Lock the third: gates to be rehung. Lock the second: chamber to be dredged. Lock the first: keeper to be retired.

npcs.name: Eel-Seller Pask
npcs.title: Freebooter
dialog: Eels, roe, reed-cord, and I'll buy any iron you pull out of the mud. The fen pays, if you don't mind the fen.

interactables.name: The Repair Orders
interactables.idle_msg: Repair orders nailed to the posts before the sluice, in the sentinels' ruled hand: 'Lock the third, gates to be rehung. Navigable by the Restoration.' Dated this season.
interactables.active_msg: You copy the orders, word for word, as the courts will want them. Everything they fix points at one morning.

interactables.name: The Works Ledger
interactables.idle_msg: The Works Ledger, open on its stand: a page for every lock between this fen and the capital, a repair order against each one, every order dated to this season, and every one marked the same way: 'navigable by the Restoration'.
interactables.active_msg: You read the season's pages through to the last. Every lock on the way to the capital is to be mended and running by one date. The house is not just being cleaned; it is being made ready to run.

raised_chamber.name: Floor levels, with the works ledger landing

npcs.name: Junn
npcs.title: The Great Granary
dialog: Wheat to the horizon, granary towers like castles, and a line of harvester sentinels working the fields in formation. It would be idyllic if any of it were for anyone.
Forty towers. I go tower to tower with the count-book; the harvesters won't mind me, but the wild things in the wheat will.

npcs.name: Duelist-Master Sabel
npcs.title: The Great Granary
dialog: For three hundred years the harvesters reaped and let it rot. This year the doors are open and the stores are filling. Somebody flipped a page in a very old plan.
You provision for two things in this world: a garrison, or a homecoming feast. Same arithmetic, different tablecloth.

npcs.name: Warden Morrow
npcs.title: The Great Granary
dialog: Forty towers full and filling. Enough to feed a city. Enough to feed their city, every man, woman and child of it, from the morning they arrive.
They're not coming back to rebuild, friends. They're coming back to resume.

npcs.name: A Count Sentinel
npcs.title: The Count
dialog: Tower the ninth: filled. Tower the tenth: filling. The count is kept.
Rations for a city, from the morning they arrive. Phase five.

npcs.name: Goodwife Tessaly
npcs.title: The Western Farm
dialog: We never left. Somebody has to farm between the harvesters' rows. Bread, apples, and I'll buy any sheaf you bring in; the sentinels don't count ours.

npcs.name: Old Harl
npcs.title: The Southern Farm
dialog: The reapers never troubled us. They reap the survey rows and leave the rest. This year they're carting it to the towers instead of letting it rot, and I don't like what that means.
The oxen went wild when the people went. They got bigger. Mind them.

interactables.name: The Count-Tables
interactables.idle_msg: The tally sentinels' count-tables before the great doors, the books open: tower by tower, filled and filling. 'Flour for the capital, phase five.'
interactables.active_msg: You copy the count. Forty towers. Enough to feed a city from the morning they arrive.

interactables.name: The Provisioning Ledger
interactables.idle_msg: The provisioning ledger on its stand: forty towers, tower by tower, filled and filling. 'Flour for the capital, phase five. Rations for a city from the morning they arrive.'
interactables.active_msg: You take the season's pages. They are not coming back to rebuild. They are coming back to resume.

raised_chamber.name: Floor levels, with the provisioning office landing

npcs.name: Duelist-Master Sabel
npcs.title: The Embassy
dialog: The courts have finally agreed on something, which frightens me more than the sentinels do. A joint embassy: formal letters from all three cities, delivered to whoever, whatever, commands in the empire's absence.
We climb the wall, we present ourselves, we do this properly. You're the honour guard. Try not to let it go to your sword arm.

npcs.name: Junn
npcs.title: The Embassy
dialog: Can I say something absurd? I spent an hour this morning deciding what to wear. To meet an empire. I settled on the archive formals, and my collar is crooked.
Three hundred years of history is about to look at me.

npcs.name: Warden Morrow
npcs.title: The Embassy
dialog: Your collar is fine. I wore the hall's oldest robe, the one with the burn from the Felling. Let history look at that.
Caretaker governments. Three hundred years of burying our own dead outside their locked door, and we're the house staff. Junn, write this down: the bill now has a cover letter.

npcs.name: The Herald Sentinel
npcs.title: The Great Watchtower
dialog: Good day. You are expected; the wall reported your climb an hour ago. I am authorised to receive correspondence addressed to the household.
I am not authorised to negotiate, apologise, or speculate, and I want to say that the restraint has been effortful.

npcs.name: A Wall Sentinel
npcs.title: The Rampart Road
dialog: The rampart road is closed to unchartered traffic. You are chartered. Proceed.
The wall is one hundred miles. It is patrolled. It has always been patrolled.

npcs.name: Wall-Runner Ketch
npcs.title: Freebooter
dialog: Ropes, pitons, and the good snow-boots. The sentinels let you on the road; they don't let you on the outer face. I do.

interactables.name: The Regent's Reply
interactables.idle_msg: A letter nailed to the post at the embassy's camp, sealed with the Regent's seal and written long before the embassy ever climbed the wall. It is addressed: 'To the caretaker governments of the free cities.'
interactables.active_msg: 'To the caretaker governments of the free cities. The household thanks you for keeping the land warm. You are asked to prepare an accounting of your stewardship, and to be ready to yield custody of the interior provinces upon the Restoration. Signed and sealed, the Regent, keeper of the capital, servant of the returning crown.'

interactables.name: The Herald's Lectern
interactables.idle_msg: The herald's lectern, and on it the reply, prepared in advance: to the caretaker governments of the free cities.
interactables.active_msg: You take the reply for the courts. The bill now has a cover letter.

portals.name: The Road to the King's Gardens
The Road to the Granary Plains

npcs.name: Junn
npcs.title: The Fire Line
dialog: The fire line is exactly where the old maps drew it, ring-shaped, wrapped around the capital like... I was going to say like a wound, but wounds are accidents.
Look at the glassed orchard. Every trunk bent away from the city. The melt ripples run outward, all of them, like rings from one dropped stone. One flash, from the centre, in a single morning.

npcs.name: Warden Morrow
npcs.title: Emmer's Farm
dialog: A farmhouse. Inside the fire line, patched and re-patched, lived in long after the burn, and a grave out front with fresh ash-flowers on it. Fresh. In this place.
There are letters on the table. Sit down and read them, all three, oldest first. I'll stand watch.

npcs.name: The Grave-Keeper Sentinel
npcs.title: Emmer's Grave
dialog: He remained on the household rolls. Residents are entitled to upkeep. I brought his chair out at noon for sixty-one years and I have continued the practice, as the instruction was never rescinded.
You are the first visitors. He would have offered you plums. I do not have plums. I regret the shortfall.

npcs.name: Duelist-Master Sabel
npcs.title: Before the Gates
dialog: There it is. The capital of Vanai. Walls without one scorch mark on them, in the middle of all this ash, and every road we've walked runs straight to those gates like spokes to a hub.
'Go home,' it says. Charming. We are not going home. We make camp right here, in sight of the gates. The ash beasts come at the light, and they'll keep coming all night.

npcs.name: Warden Morrow
npcs.title: Before the Gates
dialog: Weeks. After three hundred years, weeks. You know what frightens me? Not the Regent. Not the crown. It's that I've been the keeper of my hall's oldest grudge my whole life, and in a few weeks I have to find out what I am when it's answered.

npcs.name: Quartermaster Veil
npcs.title: The Courts' Camp
dialog: The war-chests are open. Every banner in the world is marching here, and they'll all want feeding. Take what you need; the courts are paying, for once, without arguing.

interactables.name: Emmer's Letters
interactables.idle_msg: Emmer's table, inside the fire line. Three letters lie on it, oldest first, in a farmer's plain hand. Year one, to his brother in the city: 'I walked to the walls again today and knocked until my hands bled. I slept outside the gate the night it happened, drunk in the orchard. Open the door and laugh at me.' Year forty: 'The ash orchard fruited this spring. Nobody believes me but the metal gardener, who still sets your chair out at noon. Somebody should be tending this side of the door too.' The last, to whoever opens the gate: 'I am old now and I will miss the homecoming, which is a good joke after everything, and I hope somebody laughs.'
interactables.active_msg: Emmer's table, inside the fire line. Three letters lie on it, oldest first, in a farmer's plain hand. Year one, to his brother in the city: 'I walked to the walls again today and knocked until my hands bled. I slept outside the gate the night it happened, drunk in the orchard. Open the door and laugh at me.' Year forty: 'The ash orchard fruited this spring. Nobody believes me but the metal gardener, who still sets your chair out at noon. Somebody should be tending this side of the door too.' The last, to whoever opens the gate: 'I am old now and I will miss the homecoming, which is a good joke after everything, and I hope somebody laughs. When they come back, tell them a man waited here, and was not sorry, and kept the orchard. It wasn't your fault either. Emmer.' You fold the three letters back in their order and take a fair copy for the courts; the letters themselves stay on his table, where he left them.

interactables.name: The Orchard Sighting
interactables.idle_msg: A survey post at the edge of the Glassed Orchard, with a line scored across its top to sight along. Every trunk leans away from the city; every ripple in the melted ground runs outward from it.
interactables.active_msg: You sight along the burn and record the ripple direction: outward, away from the capital. One point of three.

interactables.name: The Ridge Sighting
interactables.idle_msg: A survey post at the foot of the Melt Ridge. The glass lies piled on this side of the rise, where the melt ran up the slope from the west, from the city.
interactables.active_msg: You sight along the burn and record the ripple direction: outward, away from the capital. Two points of three.

interactables.name: The Road Cut Sighting
interactables.idle_msg: A survey post at the mouth of the Old Road Cut. The cutting's walls are glassed only on the faces that look toward the city; the faces turned away are bare stone.
interactables.active_msg: You sight along the burn and record the ripple direction: outward, away from the capital. Three points of three. Three points make a pattern, and the pattern is a centre. Take the readings to Junn at the Fire Line.

interactables.name: The Beacon Log
interactables.idle_msg: The beacon log, open on its stand at the last page. The final entry, in a calm hand: 'The household departs at the appointed hour. Lit at the signal. The fire faced outward, as instructed. The fire is ours.'
interactables.active_msg: You take the last page. As instructed: somebody wrote the instruction, and the beacon followed it.

portals.name: The Gates, to the Burned Land

npcs.name: Junn
npcs.title: The Empty City
dialog: The gates opened for us. No fanfare. The Regent just unbarred them, the way you let inspectors in when the audit can't be avoided.
A whole city, set like a table. Bread queues chalked on the bakery board. A child's game abandoned mid-move in the square. There is no dust. Someone has been dusting.

npcs.name: Duelist-Master Sabel
npcs.title: The Census Hall
dialog: Found the census hall. You should come see the census hall.

The rolls are current. Not theirs. Ours. Caerdun, Heartwood, Moonmere: three hundred years of them, updated in that same calm hand. We were never outside the empire, friends. We were the part of the household that stayed home.

npcs.name: Warden Morrow
npcs.title: The Great Stair
dialog: Kept out and kept well, all along. I have spent my life sharpening a grievance and they've spent three centuries recording my birthdays.
I don't know whether to burn something or weep, and knowing me it'll be both, alphabetically.

npcs.name: The Regent
npcs.title: Keeper of the Capital
dialog: Be welcome in the palace of Vanai. You are the first guests I have received in three hundred years, and I confess I have rehearsed. Ask. You have crossed a world to ask.

They did not go gladly, and they did not go far, and the direction they went is not one you have a word for. I stood on the walls that night. The light of every lamp in the city leaned, all one way, like grass under wind.
I must verify my instruction against this. The household guard will conduct the verification. That is the form it takes. I am sorry. It is the only form I have.

interactables.name: The Census Rolls
interactables.idle_msg: The census rolls of the household, open on their desks in the Census Hall, one volume to a city: Caerdun, Heartwood, Moonmere. Births, deaths and marriages, three hundred years of them, in the same calm hand that wrote 'Seal it behind us', and the latest entries are this spring's. Emmer, the farmer who knocked at the walls, is here. So is everyone.
interactables.active_msg: The census rolls of the household lie open on their desks in the Census Hall, one volume to a city: Caerdun, Heartwood, Moonmere. Births, deaths and marriages, three hundred years of them, in the same calm hand that wrote 'Seal it behind us'; the latest entries are this spring's, and Emmer, the farmer who knocked at the walls, is here. You find the page with your own city on it and copy it out. The names on it are your neighbours'. The free cities were never outside the empire; by its own rolls, they were the part of the household that stayed home.

interactables.name: The Bakery Board
interactables.idle_msg: The bakery board, chalked: the morning's queue, names and loaves, in a hand three hundred years old. The chalk has not been touched.
interactables.active_msg: Somebody has been dusting round the chalk.

interactables.name: The Archive
interactables.idle_msg: The archive's reading desk, and the minutes of three hundred years on it: every acre the courts hold, every year, noted for the crown's attention.
interactables.active_msg: You read the last minute. 'The caretaker governments continue in their stewardship. The Restoration is close.'

portals.name: The Gates, to the Burned Land

npcs.name: The First Minister of Vanai
npcs.title: The Palace Steps
dialog: People of the morning. Ours, and... ours, I see. Yes. We know your faces; we kept your rolls. There will be proclamations, and accountings, and more apologies than there are clerks to draft them, and they will all begin tomorrow.
You will want to know why. You are owed why. But not this morning. This morning has waited three hundred years and it will not be spent on dread. Not yet. Let us have this morning first.

npcs.name: The Regent
npcs.title: Off Duty
dialog: Do not mind me. I am off duty. I have never once been off duty, and I am given to understand one simply stands about. It is harder than the wall was.
They said it to me on the steps, before the proclamations. One word, from the crown itself, in front of the household. Relieved.

npcs.name: Warden Morrow
npcs.title: The Palace Steps
dialog: They begin now, minister. I carry the grudge hall of Heartwood: three hundred years, itemised, with interest. And my colleagues carry a wage book and an apology of our own. We've had a long time to prepare. Exactly as long as you.

npcs.name: Junn
npcs.title: The Morning
dialog: Dawn. The date. I've checked my arithmetic eleven times and Sabel confiscated my chalk.
Listen. The valley bell. All the way from the Reservoir, over the mountains, clear as a dinner call. That's a peal nobody living has ever heard.

npcs.name: Duelist-Master Sabel
npcs.title: The Morning
dialog: Between one bell-stroke and the next, the streets are full. The city does not wake. It simply stops waiting.
Two peoples on one world now. Try not to start anything before lunch.

npcs.name: Baker Ilsa
npcs.title: The Bakery
dialog: The tray's just come out. Next! Oh, you're not on the board. Well. You are now.

npcs.name: Greengrocer Tam
npcs.title: The Market
dialog: Strange faces in my square. Strange coin, too, but it's coin. What'll it be?

npcs.name: Apothecary Wren-of-the-City
npcs.title: The Market
dialog: Tinctures, powders, and something for the shock. Everyone's buying something for the shock.

npcs.name: A Market Woman
npcs.title: The Market Square
dialog: ...and so I told him, if he wants it by the morning he can... who are you? Where did you come from? Where did the morning come from?

npcs.name: A Clerk of the Archive
npcs.title: The Archive
dialog: Three hundred years of minutes to be read into the record by tomorrow. The Regent kept them. The Regent kept everything.

npcs.name: Old Stone-Player
npcs.title: The Market Square
dialog: It's my move. It's been my move for three hundred years. Don't touch the stones.

npcs.name: A Household Guard
npcs.title: The Gates
dialog: The gates stand open by order of the crown. Residents and... residents. Proceed.

npcs.name: A Chaplain
npcs.title: The Chapel
dialog: We lit every lamp that night. I remember lighting them. I remember the song. I do not remember the three hundred years, and I am told I should be grateful.

npcs.name: An Old Woman
npcs.title: The West Ward
dialog: Emmer's chair. Somebody bring Emmer's chair in from the ash. He'd have wanted to be here for this, the daft old hope that he was.

npcs.name: The Crown Broker
npcs.title: The Exchange
dialog: The crown's auction house, reopened this morning after a closure of three hundred years and one night. The ledgers balance. They always balanced.
Free-city coin is accepted. Free-city relics are, I am told, largely ours. We will discuss it tomorrow, with the proclamations.

npcs.name: Factor Ambrose Vane
dialog: Lots are called at the bell and struck at the counter. The bell has not rung in three hundred years, so this morning we are using a spoon and a cup.
Your goods, your price, my ledger. The Exchange takes three in the hundred, as it always did. The free cities call that a tax. We call it the custom of the house.
npcs.title: The Exchange

npcs.name: Factor Odile Marchbank
dialog: Every ledger on this counter balanced the night the city stopped. I have checked them twice this morning. Everything balanced but the world.
Four counters, one ledger. List it with me or with any of us; it goes up on the same board under the same balance, and the same buyer finds it.
npcs.title: The Exchange

npcs.name: Factor Tamsin Reeve
dialog: Stand where you can see the board. The lots go up as they come in, and this morning they come in from three cities that were villages when I last opened this ledger.
The balance on the tower is the sign over the houses in Caerdun, Heartwood and Moonmere as well, I am told. Good. Coin should keep one language, whatever the courts speak.
npcs.title: The Exchange

npcs.name: The Master of Arms
npcs.title: The Palace Steps
dialog: Every job of the household is taught on these steps, and the household has just been informed that it includes you. Stand in the light to take up another.
Relieved. That is what the crown said to the Regent. I have been asked to find out what one does after.

npcs.name: The Household Armourer
npcs.title: The Market Square
dialog: Household steel, forged for a morning that has now arrived. The furnaces of the Glassworks ran three centuries for these windows; my forge ran for this.
Prices in crown coin. Free-city coin is accepted at par, by proclamation, as of an hour ago.

npcs.name: The Innkeeper of the Morning
npcs.title: The Market Square
dialog: Rooms made up three hundred years ago and aired this morning. The linen is fine. The guests are strange. Everyone is strange today.
Something for the shock, love. Everyone's having something for the shock.

npcs.name: Lamplighter Corwen
npcs.title: The Gate Court
dialog: I lit these lamps at dusk, every one from Gate Street to the square, as I have done for nineteen years. I came back at dawn to put them out and found them cold. The wicks never touched, and the oil in them gone to varnish.
Three hundred years, they tell me. I have a ladder, a taper and a list. I am starting at the top of the list.

npcs.name: The Crier of the Household
npcs.title: The Gate Court
dialog: Hear the crown! I have a proclamation. I have had it since last night. It says the city will rise at the usual hour and go about its business. I read it out, and everyone laughs, and then they weep, and then they ask me to read it again.
The new proclamations come tomorrow. Today I have only the old one, and it is still true, near enough.

npcs.name: A Porter of the Gate
npcs.title: The Arrival
dialog: Those packs aren't from here. The straps are wrong, the buckles are wrong, and they smell of the sea. I have carried for the crown's guests since I was twelve, and never once for the people who came after.
A penny a pack to the inn, same as ever. They tell me the penny is worth more now. Nobody can tell me how much.

npcs.name: Goodwife Maren
npcs.title: The West Ward
dialog: I set the bread to rise last night and went to bed. This morning it had risen over the bowl, down the table and halfway to the door, and gone to stone. I mean to keep it. Nobody will believe me otherwise.
Hang the washing across the lane, I said, the morning will be fine. It was. It only took three hundred years to get here.

npcs.name: Smith Hilde Pell
npcs.title: The East Ward
dialog: I banked the forge at dusk, the way my father taught me. Raked it this morning and there were coals under the ash. Coals, after three hundred years. Either my father was a better smith than he let on, or whatever moved us took the fire along.
Your blade's made strange. Good, mind. Folded different. Leave it with me a day and it'll tell me everything the free cities learned while we slept.

npcs.name: A Watchman of the East Ward
npcs.title: The East Ward
dialog: Night watch, east ward, all quiet. That's what I wrote in the book at the third bell. I've just read it back. The ink's gone brown and the page is soft as cloth, and I still can't say it was wrong.
Orders were to keep the ward till relieved. I've been relieved. I'm told there's a lot of that going about this morning.

npcs.name: A Mother of the East Ward
npcs.title: The East Ward
dialog: One, two, three, four. One, two, three, four. I keep counting them. They are all here. They slept through it, all four, and woke up hungry, and that is the whole of it for them.
My sister married across the bay, into the free town that's a city now. If anyone there kept the name Hollin, I would like to know. I would like to know it very much.

npcs.name: Observer Hesk of Moonmere
npcs.title: The Market Square
dialog: The academy kept a calendar for three hundred years so that we would know this morning when it came. We knew it. It came. I have been writing for four hours and have not yet written a line I would let a student see.
Their clocks are right. Every clock in the city agrees, to the minute, with the night they left. We are the ones who are late.

npcs.name: A Flour Carrier
npcs.title: The Bakery Yard
dialog: Ilsa wants flour. The mill's went to dust in the sacks, so I'm buying it off a Caerdun carter at a price I'd have called theft yesterday. Yesterday was a long time ago, he says.

npcs.name: The Inn's Ostler
npcs.title: The Inn Yard
dialog: The stalls are empty. We had eleven horses in this yard last night. I keep going to the doors to feed them.
The free cities ride different stock, I'm told. Smaller, and wiser. I'll take any of them that will stand still while I learn its name.

npcs.name: A Water-Carrier
npcs.title: The West Ward Square
dialog: The wells were the first thing I checked, before I believed a word of it. Three hundred years, and the water came up sweet as yesterday. Whatever they did to us, they did it to the wells as well.

npcs.name: Tutor Brannoch
npcs.title: The West Ward Square
dialog: We stopped mid-lesson. 'The empire is the oldest thing in the world,' I said, and then I said 'and', and then it was morning. I have been trying all day to remember what came after the 'and'.
The children want to know if they must learn three hundred years of history now. I've told them yes. I have told myself the same.

npcs.name: Surveyor Ottilie Crane
npcs.title: Survey Street
dialog: The street is three fingers out from my chain. Three fingers in three hundred years: the ground settled and the city did not. I'll write it in the margin, and nobody will read it, which is the proper fate of a correction.
Your maps, the free cities' ones. May I see? You've drawn the interior from the outside in, every line a guess, and some of the guesses are better than ours.

npcs.name: A Letter Writer
npcs.title: Survey Street
dialog: Everybody in this city wants to write to somebody who isn't here. A cousin in a garrison town, a son at sea. I write them all down, and then we work out together where they ought to go.
The free cities' post will carry them, I'm told. They have a court for everything over there, and a fee for the rest.

npcs.name: Bookbinder Mirren
npcs.title: The Archive Court
dialog: The Archive's spines held. Calf, linen thread and good paste: three hundred years on the shelf and not one gathering loose. I'd like to meet the free-city binder who can say the same.
The academy across the water kept copies of our books, I hear. Copies! Bring me one. I want to see their stitching.

npcs.name: Candle-Maker Ysolde
npcs.title: The Chapel Court
dialog: We burned every candle the chapel had, that last night, down to the stubs, while they sang. This morning the stubs were still alight. Three fingers of wax, three hundred years. You explain it to me.

npcs.name: Gardener Fennick
npcs.title: The Chapel Garden
dialog: Nothing grew. That's what gets me. Not a weed between the stones. The roses are exactly as I left them, deadheaded on the right and not yet on the left. I'm going to finish the left.

npcs.name: A Petitioner of the Household
npcs.title: The Survey Gardens
dialog: I filed a petition yesterday about the drains in my street. The Offices reopen tomorrow, with the proclamations, and I mean to be first in the line. Three hundred years is long enough to wait on a drain.

npcs.name: A Herald of the Household
npcs.title: The Forecourt
dialog: I was to announce the crown at the evening reception. Then there was no evening, and no reception, and this morning the crown announced itself to the whole city from the steps. I have never been so glad to be out of work.

npcs.name: Groundskeeper Tansy
npcs.title: The Palace Gardens
dialog: Every hedge as I clipped it, every walk as I raked it, and not a leaf down in three hundred years. Lovely work, if I say so. I'd still have liked to see what it did if I let it alone.

npcs.name: The Orchard-Keeper
npcs.title: The East Ward Garden
dialog: The apples on these trees are last autumn's. Still on the branch, still red, three hundred years on. I picked one this morning. It tasted of last autumn. I don't know what I expected.

interactables.name: The Bakery Board
interactables.idle_msg: The bakery board, freshly chalked: today's queue, and three new names at the bottom in a different hand.
interactables.active_msg: Your name is on the board.

portals.name: The Keep's Door, to the Capital

interactables.name: The Empty Throne
interactables.idle_msg: The throne, on its dais, under the household's banners. Nobody has sat in it for a very long time; the cushion is new.
interactables.active_msg: You look at the throne for a while. It goes on being empty.
